messages:
Ellie: heads up — us-west gpu pool is showing sustained batching pressure since 09:12. p50/p95 latency creeping, alerts for gen-inference latency_slo_miss. looks like lots of tiny text requests are filling max_batch and preventing efficient packing. see metrics: https://grafana/redwood/d/GPUpool/us-west
Ryan: looking now. is this a max_batch cap hit or admission throttling? any obvious qlen spikes on the batcher?
Sasha: qlen is high and continuous. interestingly max_batch usage is near 100% but average batch size is small (~6 tokens avg) so we're hitting batch count limits not token limits. tiny reqs are creating many batches => GPU kernels warm/tear overhead and headroom exhaustion. :confused:
Marta: infra-bot alert summary posted at 09:15 — GPU queue depth + prefill/backlog elevated, steady for ~25m.
infra-bot: ALERT: us-west-gpu-pool batcher_queue_depth > 1200 for 25m; latency_slo breaches observed on route /v1/generate (p95 > 380ms). See runbook: https://internal/runbooks/batching-pressure
Dave: can we temporarily lower max_batch for the small-req class or add a low-latency priority lane? lowering max_batch might seem backwards but if max_batch is forcing more frequent kernel launches it can worsen tail. alternative: give small-reqs a dedicated smaller batcher with higher admission priority.
Ellie: agreed we should avoid reflexively increasing fleet size — that'll bump cost. short term we need either priority routing + small-batcher or change admission to prefer older requests (age-based).
Ryan: I ran a quick sim: if we cap per-request token cap at 64 for this route and enable age-priority, p95 drops ~30% in sim. command I ran: `python tools/sim_batching.py --trace traces/us-west-09.csv --policy age_priority --per_req_max 64`
Sasha: nice. also seeing a neutral effect from prefix caching here — lots of short unique prompts so cache miss rate high.
Marta: ops question — how feasible is a canary of a small-batcher pool? we have spare gpus in dedicated-dev but not prod. can we spin a small 4-node pool in us-west-1 for 30m trial? cost estimate?
Dave: 4 T4-equivalents for 30m is minimal infra cost, but operator time to wire up routing and rollbacks is nontrivial. I can script routing switch: `./bin/route-set --route /v1/generate --pool us-west-small-batcher --weight 0.1` and a rollback `--weight 0.0`
Ellie: let's do two-prong: (1) quick sim + apply per-request token cap 64 on the hit-heavy route (2) spin small-batcher canary at 10% traffic. if canary improves p95, we scale. Ryan/Sasha can you own sim + config? Dave/Marta own canary spin and routing.
Ryan: on it, will push sim results in 10m.
Sasha: i will prepare admission config diff: reduce global max_batch_count from 256 -> 128 for the pool and add age-priority flag. snippet: `admission: { max_batch_count: 128, priority: age }` ; will open PR and tag @Dave for rollout steps.
Marta: i'll provision canary and estimate cost. tagging billing to keep them in loop. cc @finance
Ellie: also note this might be more common in api routes with many short calls (uploads from clients vs large text completion). we should schedule a follow-up after canary for routing policies across regions. adding a 30m follow-up. :calendar:
infra-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: created ticket INF-2026-2387 (batching pressure - us-west) with owners: Ryan, Sasha, Dave, Marta.
Dave: quick mitigation idea: temporarily increase admission timeout to allow batching to wait an extra 10ms to pick up more requests; wins if traffic is bursty. i'll test in sim as well.
Ryan: sim with 10ms extra window shows slight p50 improvement but p95 only with priority + small-batcher. pushing PR for per-request cap now.
Ellie: good. next steps captured in INF-2026-2387. re-open thread if canary shows regressions. thanks team. :thumbsup:
